title: Dominic and the Passage
premise: Felix Yarrow, a salvage diver who has spent years outrunning debts, warrants, and his own history, takes a contract on a wreck the navy officially denies exists. When a government survey team vanishes from the site—leaving intact gear, sealed hatches, and no tracks—Felix realizes the wreck holds something that makes people disappear, and that his own past has already put him on someone's list. Racing a rival salvage fleet and the monsoon, he has six tides to reach the truth first. He survives by finally choosing to stop running, surfacing with evidence that costs him the anonymity he built his life on but earns him a place among the crew he once kept at arm's length.
about_author: Edmund Kavanagh is the pen name of a former merchant marine who spent a decade working coastal salvage before turning to writing. He lives in a harbor town where the tide tables matter more than the calendar.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Felix Yarrow's POV. Felix takes a salvage contract on an uncharted wreck, lying to his crew about its navy markings to keep them from walking away. The chapter establishes his rule—never stop moving—and the monsoon bearing down on the coast. Emotional beat: restless unease, the itch of a man who knows this job is too good to be clean.

chapters.title: The Survey Team's Coffee
chapters.summary: Told through crew member Priya's eyes. Diving the wreck, they find a government survey camp abandoned mid-meal—cups still warm, radios charged, boots by the tents. No tracks lead out. Priya wants to report it; Felix refuses, knowing officials ask questions he can't answer. Emotional beat: creeping dread as comfort curdles into wrongness.

chapters.title: What the Wreck Carries
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Below, Felix finds the hold sealed from the inside and a manifest listing cargo that was never cargo—people, crates of records, a name he recognizes from his own past. He realizes the navy's silence isn't embarrassment; it's protection. Emotional beat: the shock of recognition, memory dragging up what he buried.

chapters.title: Company Boats
chapters.summary: Deckhand Tomas's POV. The rival salvage fleet arrives early, flying flags that don't match any registry, and offers Felix a buyout with a threat folded inside. Tomas, who has a family ashore, urges taking the money. Felix refuses. Emotional beat: loyalty tested against fear, the first open fracture in the crew.

chapters.title: The Man Who Stopped
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. They find one survey team member alive, hiding in a sea cave—half-mad, raving that the wreck remembers everyone who touches it. He recognizes Felix's old name, proving Felix's past is already in the file someone is keeping. Emotional beat: terror of being known, the price of a life built on erasure.

chapters.title: Three Tides
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. With the monsoon three tides out, the rival fleet cuts their anchor lines in the night, and one crew member defects with their charts. Priya holds what's left together while Felix goes silent, planning. Emotional beat: grief and resolve, a crew deciding whether Felix is worth the cost of staying.

chapters.title: The Hold Opens
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix dives alone into the sealed hold and finds the survey team's fate—and the records proving the wreck was a deliberate disappearance, erased people and erased evidence in one hull. He takes the proof. Emotional beat: cold clarity; Felix understands that surfacing with this means his old life is over.

chapters.title: Monsoon Landfall
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The storm hits as the rival fleet closes in. A running battle in white water—Felix's crippled boat versus the hunters—ends when the sea itself intervenes, wrecking both pursuers on the reef they came to strip. Emotional beat: desperate, kinetic survival; Tomas choosing Felix's side at last.

chapters.title: The Price
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Ashore, Felix must decide: sell the records quietly and vanish again, or give them to the one journalist who will burn his cover name wide open. He hands them over, standing still while the consequences arrive. Emotional beat: sacrifice as release—stopping costs everything, and he pays it.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Weeks later, the crew repairs the boat in a harbor Felix would once have fled by dawn. His old name is public now; warrants and ghosts are circling. But the crew stayed, and for the first time Felix belongs somewhere he didn't buy with silence. Emotional beat: hard-won belonging, an ending that is a beginning.
